chunks: Ali, from his father, from Ibn Abu Umeyr, from Ibn Azina, from one of his companions, from one of the two Imams (peace be upon them) that
when a man leaves behind a sword and weapons, it is for his son, and if he has sons, it is for the eldest among them.
ai.seo_question: Who inherits a father's sword and weapons according to Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: This hadith from Al-Kafi highlights a specific exception to the general rule of equal distribution among heirs, establishing that a sword and weapons are inherited exclusively by the eldest son. This ruling reflects the historical context where weapons were considered tools of trade or status rather than mere chattel, warranting a distinct inheritance path to preserve martial capability within the family line. It underscores the Shia scholarly understanding of 'khas' (specific) items having unique inheritance rules compared to general assets.

en.hubeali:
Ali, from his father, from Ibn Abu Umeyr, from Ibn Azina, from one of his companions, 
(It has been narrated) from one of the two<sup>asws</sup> (5<sup>th</sup> or 6<sup>th</sup> Imam<sup>asws</sup>)
that the man, when he leaves (as legacy), a sword and weapons, so it is for his son, and if there were two sons for him, so it is for the eldest one’.
en.sarwar: 2. Ali ibn Ibrahim has narrated from his father from ibn abu ‘Umayr from ibn ’Udhaynah from certain persons of his people who has narrated the following: “One of the two Imam, (abu Ja‘far or abu ‘Abd Allah), ‘Alayhim al-Salam, has said, ‘
If a man leaves behind a sword and arms and sons, such items belong to the eldest son.”’
